Definition: the Apportioner, i.e. Fate (as an idol)
BiblicalUsage: Meni is the Apportioner, the god Fate, whom the Jews in Babylon worshipped. Isaiah 65:11 rebukes those who forsake the LORD and prepare a table for that troop, and furnish the drink offering unto that number, the King James rendering of the god's name.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Fate is the poorest god of all: it promises nothing, gives nothing, and takes the worship that belongs to the LORD.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
